You can now use BTC for a U.S. home down payment without selling it.

@betrmortgage lets you pledge BTC and use part of its value toward the down payment, while the rest of the purchase goes through a standard mortgage.

A few details on how it works:

→ $250K in BTC can support a $100K down payment
→ BTC price drops don’t trigger margin calls or require additional collateral
→ Better holds the BTC in custody through @coinbase
→ The BTC is returned once the down-payment loan is repaid

Just know that Better can liquidate the BTC after 60 days of missed payments.

So in practice, you’re still taking a normal mortgage. The BTC is just helping cover the down payment without forcing you to sell it.

One trade-off: every $1 of down-payment credit requires $2.50 in BTC.

I can see the appeal if you want to keep your BTC exposure while buying a home.

tweets.text:
The psychology of every “we’re so back” cycle:

Majors pump.

↓

Shorts get liquidated. The squeeze sends prices higher.

↓

Prices keep climbing. Confidence slowly returns.

↓

Trading picks up. People start posting PnLs again.

↓

The feed starts filling with everyone winning. Being sidelined starts hurting.

↓

FOMO kicks in. Sideliners start buying.

↓

Profits from majors flow into riskier assets and leveraged longs.

↓

Bigger wins, more PnL sharing, more people chasing.

↓

Winning feels easy. Leverage amounts progress.

↓

Everyone raises their targets instead of taking profits.

↓

The first dump gets bought. The bounce brings another wave of FOMO.

↓

More shorts get liquidated. Bears are fcked. Bulls are in control.

↓

The next dip barely bounces. Trading gets harder.

↓

Overleveraged longs get liquidated. Forced selling triggers more liquidations.

↓

PnL screenshots are getting rarer. It's now liquidation data.

↓

FOMO flips from fear of missing gains to fear of losing what’s left.

↓

Everyone turns bearish again.

⚡ THE DAILY METALS PULSE — 28 AUGUST 2026 ⚡

Four metals. One pulse. No noise.

The market is waiting for one speech.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh addresses Jackson Hole later today. DXY is near a one-week high at 99.13, the US 10-year yield is around 4.68%, and markets see roughly a 34% chance of a September rate hike, rising to 74% by December.

☢️ URANIUM

Uranium continues to hold around the $90/lb level while the nuclear buildout keeps accelerating.

The US Army has selected five microreactor developers for deployment at five military bases under its $2.2 billion Janus Program.

In Sweden, Fortum’s NuCore has applied for state support for 1.2–3.4 GW of new nuclear capacity at Oskarshamn.

From military bases to national power grids, future uranium demand continues moving from ambition toward funded programs and formal projects.

🟠 COPPER

Copper is trading around $6.60/lb, only about 3% below August’s record.

Chile and Argentina have now approved operating protocols for Vicuña, NexoAndino and Filo Sur. Their revived cross-border framework could unlock $20.7 billion in investment and eventually add 540,000 tonnes of annual copper production.

That is a major supply response, but one measured in years rather than quarters. The world needs more copper now.

🥈 SILVER

Silver is down around 1% near $68.50 as elevated yields and the firmer dollar weigh on precious metals.

The important resistance zone remains $70.60–$72. A hawkish Warsh could prolong the consolidation, while a softer or more balanced message could give silver another attempt at breaking through.

Today’s weakness is macro-driven. The structural silver deficit has not disappeared.

🥇 GOLD

Gold has eased to around $4,576 after reaching a three-month high earlier this week.

Higher-for-longer rate fears are creating short-term pressure, but ETF participation, official-sector buying and concerns over US fiscal credibility continue to provide support.

A hawkish speech could produce another dip. A balanced one could quickly bring $5,000 back into focus.

Today’s trigger is monetary policy. The structural cases for all four metals continue building underneath the noise.

#uranium #nuclear $M.CN $MYRUF

☢️ What if America’s largest uranium project was already drilled, planned for production and then abandoned for nearly half a century?

That may be the story of Myriad Uranium’s Copper Mountain.

In the 1970s, Union Pacific drilled around 2,000 boreholes, identified seven historic deposits and invested the equivalent of approximately C$125 million.

A six-pit conventional mine was planned, with production scheduled for 1983.

Then Three Mile Island crushed the uranium market and Copper Mountain was shelved.

The geology did not fail. The uranium market did.

Now uranium is around $90/lb, nuclear power is surging and Washington wants a domestic fuel supply. Ironically, a reactor at the Three Mile Island site is being restarted through a 20-year agreement with Microsoft.

Myriad now owns 100% of this 18,000+ acre project in Wyoming, America’s leading uranium jurisdiction.

A 1982 U.S. Department of Energy assessment outlined conceptual potential for 245–655 Mlbs eU₃O₈. This is historical and not a current resource, but it shows the extraordinary district-scale potential.

Phase II drilling is now testing that thesis. At Lucky Cliff, all four holes encountered broad, shallow uranium mineralization outside every historical resource or endowment area.

Copper Mountain was not abandoned because it lacked uranium.

It was abandoned because it arrived at the wrong time.

Myriad may be bringing it back at exactly the right one.

Disclosure: Paid partnership with Myriad Uranium. Always do your own research.

Crypto always felt like it was made for the age were going into, not the age we came from.

@ErikVoorhees nails it in this clip... this is truly natively digital money and we invented it for machines that hadnt come around yet.

Look at everything that held back adoption. Private keys, seed phrases, the cryptography... all hard for humans. The UX has been the industrys biggest struggle from day one. All that stuff is completely native to an agent. The exact things humans fight with are trivial for them.

Almost like it was preordained for something else than we originally thought.

tweets.text:
In seven or eight years there'll be gigantic hedge funds that nobody can see. They wont have an office or a star trader on the front page of the FT... the whole operation will be agents running capital through the liquidity layer.

Think about what a hedge fund is. A group of managers allocating capital to pods of traders. Every one of those pods can be an agent on chain... your relative value bond agent, your equity arb agent, your long short agent. That alone strips out something like 90% of the cost of allocating capital.

Then the mothership. Risk management, compliance, capital raising... AI eats all of that too. You can apply it to every asset management business on earth. 

An invisible economy is coming, and all of it inevitably happens onchain. DeFi is the obvious venue.

tweets.text:
Einstein loved thought experiments. So, here is a fiscal one:

You are the parent of 4 children. They are locked in separate rooms with a Zoom feed to you. For the sake of this experiment, there is 0% hope of miraculous escape. 

You are told that one must be chosen for death. 

Otherwise, no food or water will be given to any of them. All four will simply die of thirst in a matter of days.

But, if you chose one, the other 3 will be set free. And not only that, they will be handed multi-million trust funds. 

Clearly, what most people would do is try to find an escape, then watch as their children weaken. But once it becomes clear that all will soon die unless a choice is made, the next logical step is to choose, as horrible as that is.  

Here are the four fiscal children:

-Social Security
-Medicare
-Defense
-The Bond market (partially owned by foreigners and largely owned by wealthy individuals and pension holders (in other words, a minority of the US population)) & currency (inflation) - (however, please note that given most Americans are in debt--should wages keep up with inflation--they will actually benefit with a reduction in the real value of their debt).

In other words, chose the bond market/currency, most Americans actually win so long as real wages don't decline. 

Who do you choose to die?
